entries.summary: Wave 1 intentionally defers DrawImage and the full platform image bridge; Mirage records a curated canvas subset first and leaves image drawing for Wave 2.

Wave 1 records deterministic DrawString commands, falls back to plain text content for DrawText(IAttributedText, ...), and still defers GetStringSize, attributed span styling, justified text, and broader overflow/layout fidelity on the browser canvas backend.

Wave 1 replays solid, linear, and radial fill paints through the current ICanvas surface, while non-solid stroke paint breadth remains deferred until a browser-compatible stroke-paint strategy is added in a follow-up wave.
Wave 1 supports rectangle clip commands for deterministic canvas replay but still defers ClipPath, SubtractFromClip, and path-measurement breadth to the follow-up wave.
Mirage uses the native browser canvas engine for text and shadow replay, so exact Android/iOS glyph metrics and shadow rendering can differ while staying deterministic for the supported subset.
